fields.label: First VRAM tile reserved for half-width text
fields.description: First background tile index (0-255) reserved for composed character-pair tiles. Must not overlap tiles used by the scene background (0 to 191 depending on the scene) or the UI/dialogue tiles (192-255).

fields.label: Last VRAM tile reserved for half-width text
fields.description: Last background tile index (inclusive) reserved for composed character-pair tiles. At most 64 tiles are used even if the range is larger.

fields.label: Tile placement (VRAM bank)
fields.description: Which VRAM tile data bank the composed pair tiles are uploaded to. 'Bank 1 only' and 'Alternate' are Game Boy Color features (Color Only mode, or Color modes running on GBC): they free up or double the bank 0 budget by storing pair tiles in bank 1, selected per tilemap cell through attribute bit 3. On DMG hardware the plugin always falls back to bank 0. Alternate placement doubles the pairs a given tile range can hold.

fields.label: Enable pair-tile cache
fields.description: When enabled, composed pair tiles are tracked in an LRU cache so a pair that was already drawn reuses its tile instead of consuming a new one. Disable it to compile the cache out: every pair is then composed into the next tile of the reserved range, cycling round-robin. That reclaims all of the cache WRAM (4 bytes per entry) and skips the lookup, but each pair is recomposed on every use and the reserved range must be large enough for all pairs visible at once (half the characters of the longest page), otherwise tiles still on screen get overwritten.

fields.label: Pair cache capacity (entries)
fields.description: Maximum number of character pairs the LRU cache can track. Each entry costs 4 bytes of WRAM and, when in use, one VRAM tile from the reserved range. The usable entry count at runtime is the smaller of this value and the reserved tile range size. Lower it to reclaim WRAM, raise it only alongside a larger reserved tile range. Ignored when the pair-tile cache is disabled: the whole reserved range is then used.

fields.label: Replace stock text rendering
fields.description: Compile GB Studio's own text renderer out of the ROM and point everything that used it at this plugin instead. The stock Display Dialogue, Display Text and Menu events then draw in 4px-wide text, without being replaced by this plugin's own events. Two things follow. Tiles 204-255, which the stock renderer used as its scratch buffer, are free: they can be added to this plugin's reserved tile range with nothing left to collide with. Menus are unaffected: this plugin's lines are one map row tall, like stock text, so the stock menu cursor already lines up.
